Mission condos for sale: apartment-style homes in strata buildings. The Fraser Valley Real Estate Board benchmark for apartments (condos) in Mission was $396,200 in October 2026 (-8.2% over a year). Before you offer, read the strata documents: the depreciation report, meeting minutes, bylaws and fees.
Mission condos sold, November 2025 to October 2026

36 condos sold in Mission with a median price of $468,250 (the middle half sold between $400,000 and $519,750), taking a median of 32 days to sell at 97.6% of the last list price; 3% sold above list. They had a median $496 per square foot, a median year built of 2006 and a median strata fee of $433 a month.

blocks.text: Mission Condos: streets and boundaries

items.t: Mission's condo stock is small and central: almost every apartment building stands in the urban core around 1st Avenue, 2nd Avenue, Horne Street and Stave Lake Street, below the hillside neighbourhoods.

Mission City Station at 33200 North Railway Avenue is the transit anchor at the core's south edge, and the Mission Leisure Centre at 7650 Grand Street and Mission Memorial Hospital at 7324 Hurd Street are the central amenities the buildings cluster around.

blocks.text: Mission Condos: the housing stock

items.t: The new shelf is one developer deep: Redekop Faye built Preston on Fourteenth at 32690 14th Avenue (2023, 103 condominiums plus 11 affordable rental homes), Montgomery at 7375 Horne Street and Silver & Cedar at 8423 Cedar Street in Cedar Valley — three of the city's newest apartment buildings share one builder.
Montgomery is six storeys and 85 homes on the developer's own page, marketed at 7375 Horne Street while resale listings address units at 33281 2 Avenue — the same building carrying two addresses.

Two complexes buyers find in "condo" feeds are actually townhome stratas: Cherry Lane at 32165 Seventh Avenue (built 1989, 22 homes) and Luther Place at 7525 Martin Place / 32286 7th Avenue (built 1988, 36 homes, a 55+ complex) — they belong to the townhome shelf, not this page's apartment stock.

blocks.text: Mission Condos: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Mission replaced its Official Community Plan (OCP) this year: OCP Bylaw 6405-2026 was adopted June 1, 2026, replacing Bylaw 6350-2025, and zoning runs under Zoning Bylaw 5949-2020 — any condo document or listing citing the old OCP is a bylaw out of date.

Only a 55-or-older residency bylaw is legal in a British Columbia strata (Strata Property Act sections 123.1 and 123.2), with exemptions for legacy residents, live-in caregivers and, since May 1, 2023, younger spouses or partners and defined children — the frame for Briskham Manor's and Luther Place's 55+ rules, to be confirmed on the Form B.

Long-term rental restriction bylaws have been unenforceable since November 24, 2022, so a directory line saying "rentals not allowed" at an older Mission building is old bylaw text, not current law; short-term rentals can still be restricted, and one Glenkirk Court listing states "No short term rentals."

Every Mission strata of five or more lots must now obtain a depreciation report every five years with no deferral vote (in force July 1, 2024), and must contribute at least 10 percent of the operating fund to the contingency reserve fund — the two rules that drive levies in the 1975–1993 stock.

Developer sales at Montgomery and Silver & Cedar are presale contracts under the Real Estate Development Marketing Act (REDMA), which gives a seven-day rescission period from the later of signing and acknowledging the disclosure statement, with deposits held in trust.

blocks.text: Mission Condos: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Mission runs a three-tier school system — elementary Kindergarten to Grade 6, middle school Grades 7 to 9, secondary Grades 10 to 12 in School District 75 — so a family buying a two-bedroom condo here feeds a middle school that a Maple Ridge buyer would not expect; run the building's address through the district locator.

Preston on Fourteenth's rentals rest on a housing agreement, not just the 2022 law change: its presale record states condo rentals were permitted for 100 years, a project-level term that survives independently of the province voiding rental bylaws.
Briskham Manor's strata fee includes gas and hot water per its listing record — a real offset when comparing its fee against Mission Manor or Glenkirk Court, and a detail no fee table shows.
Mission's tax penalty is a single flat 10 percent, while some Fraser Valley rural areas use a staged scheme — the figure quoted for a Mission address must be the City one.
The City mails the 2026 tax notice in the last week of May with a July 2, 2026 due date, and owners are responsible for paying whether or not the notice arrives.

blocks.text: Mission Condos: development and new projects

items.t: Montgomery, 7375 Horne Street (also addressed as 33281 2 Avenue), Redekop Faye — six-storey condominium building of 85 homes; status: developer page live and building completing in 2026 per the developer's own site (as of November 3, 2026); no price or sold-out claim is made here.
Preston on Fourteenth, 32690 14th Avenue, Redekop Faye — four-storey building of 103 condominiums plus 11 affordable rental homes; status: completed 2023, now resale stock.

blocks.text: Mission Condos: costs and taxes

items.t: Mission sets its municipal rates by a tax rate bylaw adopted before May 15 each year, and levies additional taxes for diking — the diking levy is a Mission-specific line a condo buyer sees on the tax bill.

The City's 2026 utility figures in its budget material are flat-rate water $627.24, sewer $776.64, refuse collection $164.04 and recycling/compost $292.80 for a serviced household — from the City's 2026 budget presentation, read as budget figures, not a condo's strata-billed share.

blocks.text: Mission Condos: getting around

items.t: The West Coast Express is the rail link: Mission City Station at 33200 North Railway Avenue is the line's eastern terminus, trains run weekday mornings to Waterfront Station and back in the afternoon, and TransLink's timetable states no weekend or statutory holiday service.

BC Transit's Central Fraser Valley system runs Mission's local buses, including route 31 Valley Connector to Abbotsford via the Abbotsford-Mission Highway, route 32 West Heights, route 33 Cedar Valley, route 34 East Side, route 35 Hatzic and route 39 Shopper Shuttle.
TransLink route 701 also provides limited weekday trips to and from Mission City Station, per the West Coast Express timetable notes.
Mission is outside TransLink's tax area for most services — there is no TransLink levy line on a Mission tax bill, unlike a Surrey or Langley bill.

blocks.text: Mission Condos: risks and due diligence

items.t: For the 1975–1993 resale stock, the Form B Information Certificate and the current depreciation report are the central diligence documents — they show the contingency reserve fund balance and planned work that decide future special levies.
Confirm zoning and OCP designation for a specific condo parcel against Zoning Bylaw 5949-2020 and the new OCP Bylaw 6405-2026, not the replaced Bylaw 6350-2025.
What the City pages do not tell a buyer: a specific strata's insurance deductible for water damage or flood — that figure is in the strata's own documents obtained on a purchase.
